transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-06-23 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (DataHarbor CTO), Aisha Khan (DataHarbor ML Eng), Liam O'Neill (DataHarbor Infra)

Summary: quick scoping call to align on benchmark planning and harness integration for the POC. Focus areas: workload sizing, streaming vs non-streaming behavior, customer scripts integration, load testing parameters, success criteria and timelines.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intro, I'm Jordan, AE on the account, with Priya from solutions engineering.
[00:10] Carlos: hey thanks, i'm Carlos, CTO at DataHarbor, appreciate the time.
[00:15] Priya: hi all, quick agenda — define success metrics for the POC, align on harness integration, talk about streaming vs non-streaming and load patterns, set timeline and next steps.
[00:30] Aisha: sounds good, we have a pretty busy week so we'll keep it tight.

[02:10] Jordan: to start — high level, how are you planning to use inference in prod? what are the key perf numbers you need?
[02:20] Carlos: primary use is document summarization and reranking for our search pipeline. Latency matters — p95 under 700ms ideally, and we need to support about 60 concurrent users with burst to 200. Cost is obviously a factor.
[02:40] Aisha: also want to measure token throughput for large batch jobs — nightly jobs that run bulk summarization of 10k docs. So both low-latency interactive and high-throughput batch are needed.

[04:05] Priya: great, that's exactly why we're proposing benchmark runs in two modes: streaming (for interactive summarization where tokens come out progressively) and non-streaming full-response runs (for batch and reranking). The harness supports both.
[04:25] Liam: a quick infra note — we'll likely test against your hosted endpoint first but also want to try Dedicated later; we have VPC peering options. Security is important — SOC2, KMS, audit logs for the Dedicated runs.

[06:00] Jordan: noted. Success criteria suggestions from our side: interactive e2e p95 latency <700ms for typical 512-token prompts in streaming mode, for non-streaming p95 <1.2s for 1024 token responses, throughput target for batch of at least 2000 tokens/sec sustained on the Dedicated config you pick. Also quality check: model outputs should match baseline metrics — we can use your sample eval set for BLEU/ROUGE or embedding-distance checks.
[06:40] Carlos: that seems reasonable. how do we ensure the harness reads our scripts exactly? our prompts have some template logic and some tool-calling style JSON.

[07:20] Priya: the harness accepts customer scripts in two ways: 1) raw prompt files + a small shim that templatizes variables, or 2) a small adapter that calls your internal wrapper endpoints. For tool-calling style JSON, we can capture the calls as structured input in the harness and either replay them as full prompts or test via function-calling emulation. We'll need a few sample scripts to map.
[08:05] Aisha: ok i'll prepare three representative prompt scripts: one short chat-like, one 512-token summarization, one long-form 1k+ tokens; plus a small sample dataset.

[09:00] Jordan: perfect, for load testing parameters — we suggest starting with a baseline run: 1 client, single-threaded, 1000 requests to warm caches and measure cold/warm behavior. Then ramp to 4 and 8 concurrent clients for interactive latency profiles, and a separate batch run with high concurrency for throughput. We'll capture p50/p90/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost estimate per 1M tokens.

[11:10] Priya: important note — prefix/KV caching will affect latency significantly for interactive sessions. If your app reuses context across requests we should enable prefix caching. For the harness, we can simulate session reuse patterns and measure delta.
[12:00] Liam: good point, our product does reuse context across sessions sometimes. we'll document typical session lengths and reuse rates.

[13:30] Carlos: what's the difference we should expect between streaming and non-streaming runs in the harness?
[13:40] Priya: streaming reduces perceived latency for users because tokens arrive incrementally; from a server perspective, there's more small writes and TLS overhead but less peak memory if you stream as you generate. Non-streaming will collect the full output before responding, which can be slightly faster raw-throughput for some kernels but increases tail latency for interactive workloads. We'll measure both. For benchmarks we report both e2e user-perceived latency (first token, last token) and total server processing time.

[16:00] Jordan: on models — do you have a model in mind? open or private? the runtime supports multiple variants and we'll pick one that matches your quality/cost target.
[16:15] Aisha: currently we're prototyping with an open Llama-like family; quality baseline is our in-house reference. We may later move to a quantized variant for Dedicated.

[17:10] Priya: fine — we'll include quantized runs (4-bit/8-bit) as part of the harness to show cost/throughput tradeoffs. We'll also include a fallback variant in routing to evaluate graceful degradation.

[18:30] Carlos: security & compliance checklist — we'll need SOC2 docs, SSO options, KMS integration details. For Dedicated, audit logs and retention policies are critical.
[18:50] Jordan: we'll send the security pack and a Dedicated checklist; Priya will include notes on KMS and HSM options.

[19:20] Aisha: about metrics, can the harness output cost estimates? we want a per-request cost approximation so we can compare Hosted vs Dedicated.
[19:30] Priya: yes, the harness plugins compute token counts and we run cost models — we can produce cost per 1k tokens and projected monthly spend based on your traffic profile.

[21:00] Liam: network — when we test Dedicated in VPC, what's the expected network setup? do you support VPC peering or private link?
[21:15] Jordan: we support VPC peering and private endpoints; we'll include the network diagrams in the runbook. For initial runs we can use public endpoints with IP allowlist.

[22:30] Priya: timeline proposal: share harness + runbook (Jordan) by 2026-06-25; customer shares scripts/datasets by 2026-06-29; Redwood prepares streaming/non-streaming configs and test matrix by 2026-06-30; run initial hosted benchmark on 2026-07-02; follow-up review call on 2026-07-06 to go over results and next steps for Dedicated POC.

[24:10] Carlos: that works. are there any gotchas you typically see?
[24:20] Priya: a couple: 1) mismatch in prompt templating — we often need a small adapter to preserve whitespace/metadata; 2) session reuse assumptions — if we don't simulate reuse rates tail latency looks better than reality; 3) function-calling/tool integrations can add variability; we recommend instrumenting and recording raw input/outputs for the first runs.

[26:00] Aisha: good to know. for reporting, can we get raw logs and summarized CSVs?
[26:10] Priya: yes, harness will produce raw event logs, aggregated latency histograms, GPU metrics, and cost CSVs. We can also push results to a shared S3 if you prefer.

[28:00] Jordan: quick note on acceptance criteria: 1) interactive p95 <700ms in streaming mode for 512 tokens, 2) non-streaming p95 <1.2s for 1024 tokens, 3) batch throughput >=2000 tokens/sec for nightly job under Dedicated trial, 4) no functional regressions vs your baseline eval (we'll run the stored eval set). If those are met we recommend moving to a 4-week Dedicated pilot.

[30:10] Carlos: agreed, that covers the major points. one more question — can the harness simulate gradual traffic spikes over hours? we want to see autoscaling behavior.

[30:25] Priya: yes, it can do ramp tests over arbitrary windows and we can include autoscaling policies for Dedicated to test scale-up times and cold-start behavior.

[32:00] Aisha: for the dataset, any constraints on PII? we can't share real PII — we'll provide anonymized samples or synthetic equivalents.
[32:10] Jordan: totally fine, synthetic/anonymized is preferred for the initial runs. We'll note that in the runbook.

[33:30] Liam: who will own the run orchestration on Redwood side?
[33:40] Jordan: Priya will be the SE lead and will run the harness with the customer-provided inputs. I'll coordinate logistics and the security pack.

[34:10] Priya: I'll prepare three run configs: warm/cold baseline, streaming interactive matrix (1/4/8 clients), and batch throughput with quantized model variants.

[35:00] Jordan: ok — next steps recap: Jordan share harness repo + security docs; Aisha upload scripts and small dataset; Priya prepare run configs and run initial hosted tests; schedule follow-up on 2026-07-06.

[36:20] Carlos: great — any blockers we should flag now?
[36:30] Aisha: only internal scheduling, but we should be able to hit the timeline.

[37:00] Jordan: perfect. we'll send the invite for the 7/6 follow-up and the links in an email.

[37:20] Carlos: thanks everyone.

[37:30] (crosstalk)
[38:00] End meeting
